This week's full edition all five numbers, sources, methodology notes, and context:
austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

If you work in this space and have ICE detention numbers you can share, I want to hear from you; on or off the record.

Each of these numbers has a source. Each has a limitation. None of them tells the full story on its own, that's why I track them week to week. The full breakdown with citations is in my newsletter, posted Thursday May 22.

288 detainees at Delaney Hall in Newark signed a letter this week describing medical neglect, contagious illness spreading through shared housing, and people held past approved release dates. This is the second collective grievance letter from that facility in three months.
ICE's own inspections found 19 instances of facilities failing to meet ICE's own suicide prevention standards since January 2025.

Five people have died by suicide in ICE detention so far in 2026. That's the highest annual total in at least two decades and the year isn't half over. Nine total since the start of Trump's second term.

Fines at this scale, even uncollected, can bar people from opening bank accounts, accessing credit, or signing leases. That's the mechanism: making daily life untenable enough to induce departure without formal deportation. Public comment period runs through June 22.

DHS published a proposed rule on May 20 to raise deportation fines from $5,130 to $18,000 per person. The Federal Register notice shows DHS has already issued $36 billion in fines to roughly 65,000 people since Jan, averaging $553,000 per person.

I don't have one explanation for the decline. Courts ordering bond hearings, shifting enforcement priorities, and the DHS partial funding shutdown may all be factors. But the deeper problem is structural: Congress needs to fix ICE's data transparency, not just watch the gap grow.

ICE's biweekly detention data is now over a month old. The public currently has no official count of how many people are in ICE detention. People I trust in this space are telling me the number is under 60,000 (possibly 57,000–58,000) but that's not publicly verifiable right now.

These are American citizens, not immigration cases. Disrupted schooling, lost parental income, potential foster care, possible removal to countries they've never lived in. The methodology is conservative, meaning the real number could be higher.

Brookings researchers cross-referenced ICE arrest data with ACS demographic data to estimate that at least 145,000 U.S. citizen children have had a parent detained since January 2025. ICE doesn't report family data, so cross-referencing is the only way to estimate this at all.

This week's immigration numbers: 145,000 U.S. citizen children with a detained parent. 5 suicides in ICE custody in 2026 alone. An $18,000 proposed deportation fine. Here's what each figure actually means. 🧵

Veteran Danitza James explains how it's possible that she served this country during two tours in Iraq and still left the military without citizenship. This should not happen. Ever. 

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

Video
Thread above: @rep_our_pat @afghanevac @ChamberlainVets

If you are working on this topic, refer to these interviews for a wealth of insight and inspiration. If you have suggestions/resources for me please send them. I don’t have a lot of data (yet) on this topic, but I will share what I find. DM for interviewee emails.

Thanks you. 🇺🇸

I spoke with Danitza James of Repatriate Our Patriots, an Iraq War vet who left the Army without citizenship and now fights for impacted military families/veterans. Danitza knows of at least 45 deported veterans who have died abroad.

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

I spoke with legal legend Margaret Stock, author of the MAVNI program, about why protecting America’s national security requires more immigration—not kicking immigrants out—and the shoddy government legal work she is fighting in court every day. 

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

I spoke with Chris Purdy of the Chamberlain Network who is concerned about the politicization of the military (including the use of bases as detention centers) and sends a clear, inspiring message that no single political party or ideology owns the flag. 

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

I spoke with Shawn VanDiver of #AfghanEvac about the abandonment of our allies in Afghanistan and why this isn’t just about Afghans —  it’s about Americans showing up for what’s right and telling lawmakers on both side of the isle to find their courage. 

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

Most Americans have no clue about any of this. That’s why I sat down with 4 vets who are working at the intersection of military and immigration. The conversations are substantive, informative, and non-partisan, a great resource for anyone trying to understand the issues.
